name: Battle of Chosin Reservoir

location.terrain_description: High-altitude reservoir plateau surrounded by the Taebaek Mountains; treeless ridges, frozen roads, temperatures as low as -40°C

outcome: UN forces successfully broke out to Hungnam under sustained Chinese encirclement; strategic UN withdrawal completed
result_summary: Tactical Chinese victory (encirclement achieved); Operational UN success (14,000+ troops and 98,000 refugees evacuated at Hungnam)

factions.name: UN Command — X Corps
factions.full_name: United States X Corps + Allied Forces
factions.commander: Major General Oliver P. Smith (1st Marine Division)

factions.name: PVA 9th Army Group
factions.full_name: Chinese People's Volunteer Army — 9th Army Group

phases.label: Initial Contact & PVA Night Assault
phases.summary: X Corps pushes north toward the Yalu River, unaware that 12 PVA divisions have secretly infiltrated the Taebaek Mountains. At 2200hrs on Nov 27, the PVA launches a coordinated night assault across the entire Chosin perimeter.
phases.tactical_situation: UN forces are strung out along the Main Supply Route (MSR) from Koto-ri north through Hagaru-ri to Yudam-ni. The 5th and 7th Marine Regiments are at Yudam-ni; 1st Marines hold Hagaru-ri and Koto-ri. Task Force Faith occupies the east side of the reservoir.

events.label: PVA Night Assault Begins
events.description: At 2200hrs, 67,000 PVA troops launch a coordinated bugle-signaled assault from surrounding ridges — one of history's most dramatic night attacks.

events.label: MG Smith Orders Perimeter Defense
events.description: General Smith, who had prophetically pre-positioned supplies at Hagaru-ri against orders, activates defensive perimeter plans. His caution, mocked before the battle, now saves thousands of lives.

events.label: MSR Cut North of Koto-ri
events.description: PVA forces sever the Main Supply Route, isolating UN positions into separate pockets. Temperature drops to -35°C.

phases.annotation: The PVA's surprise infiltration — 120,000 troops hidden in mountains through arctic conditions for two weeks with minimal resupply — remains one of the most extraordinary feats of operational concealment in modern warfare.

phases.label: The Encirclement
phases.summary: UN forces are now fully encircled. Task Force Faith on the east side is systematically destroyed. The 5th and 7th Marines at Yudam-ni fight off wave attacks while Hagaru-ri — the critical logistics hub with the airstrip — is defended by a scratch force of clerks, cooks, and engineers.
phases.tactical_situation: Each UN position forms its own 360° defensive perimeter. Air supply from Marine aircraft and USAF C-119s becomes the only lifeline. The Hagaru-ri airstrip, hastily bulldozed from frozen ground, becomes the most important 2,900 feet of runway in the Korean War.

events.label: Task Force Faith Overrun
events.description: Without tank support or adequate artillery, RCT-31 under LTC Don Faith (KIA during the breakout) is destroyed as an organized unit. ~1,000 survivors reach Hagaru-ri across the frozen reservoir. Faith is posthumously awarded the Medal of Honor.

events.label: Hagaru-ri Airstrip Operational
events.description: Engineers and Korean laborers complete the emergency airstrip under fire. Over the next week, 4,312 casualties are evacuated and 537 replacement troops flown in — a logistical miracle under fire.

events.label: Marine Corsairs Establish Air Umbrella
events.description: VMF-312 and VMF-214 Corsairs fly continuous close air support. Napalm drops on PVA assault waves — in -35°C conditions, many PVA soldiers freeze to death on the ridges between attacks.

events.label: Battle of East Hill (Turkey Hill)
events.description: PVA seizes East Hill overlooking Hagaru-ri. Captain Sitter leads a counterattack retaking the hill — receives Medal of Honor. Control of the high ground preserves the perimeter.

phases.annotation: The PVA, despite 4:1 numerical superiority, lacked artillery coordination, air support, and resupply. Their soldiers suffered catastrophic frostbite casualties — entire battalions rendered combat-ineffective by cold before engaging. The Chinese later called this their most costly campaign of the entire Korean War.

phases.label: Yudam-ni Breakout to Hagaru-ri
phases.summary: The 5th and 7th Marines at Yudam-ni receive orders to fight their way south 14 miles to Hagaru-ri. This nighttime movement under sustained PVA attack — with Marines carrying their dead and wounded — becomes one of the most celebrated fighting retreats in USMC history.
phases.tactical_situation: Two Marine regiments (~8,000 men) must fight down a single-lane frozen mountain road through multiple PVA blocking positions. They bring all weapons, equipment, and casualties. No one is left behind.

events.label: Yudam-ni Column Moves Out
events.description: At 0800hrs, the column of 8,000+ Marines and 1,500 casualties begins the 14-mile march. Advance guard clears ridgelines while rear guard fights off pursuit.

events.label: Hell Fire Valley Ambush
events.description: PVA ambush catches Drysdale's Task Force (41 Commando + Marines + Army) at a narrow valley. Of 922 men, 162 are killed, 159 wounded, 256 captured. Tank-led survivors press through to Hagaru-ri.

events.label: 5th and 7th Marines Enter Hagaru-ri
events.description: After 59 hours of continuous combat movement, the Yudam-ni regiments arrive at Hagaru-ri. Smith consolidates the full division for the final push south.

phases.annotation: General Smith's famous remark to a reporter: 'Retreat, hell! We're not retreating, we're just advancing in a different direction.' This phrase defines the ethos of the entire Chosin campaign — offensive spirit maintained under the most extreme conditions of modern warfare.

phases.label: Breakout to Hungnam
phases.summary: The consolidated Marine division, with Army survivors and allied forces, fights 78 miles south from Hagaru-ri through Koto-ri and Funchilin Pass to the port of Hungnam. A treadway bridge section is airdropped to span the critical gap at Funchilin Pass — an engineering feat never attempted before or since.
phases.tactical_situation: The PVA 26th Army attempts to cut off the column at Funchilin Pass — a 4,000-foot elevation, single-file road clinging to a cliff face. The critical bridge has been destroyed. Without a crossing, 14,000 men and all equipment are trapped.

events.label: Treadway Bridge Airdrop at Funchilin Pass
events.description: USAF C-119 Flying Boxcars airdrop eight treadway bridge sections to span the destroyed Funchilin Pass bridge. Marines and engineers assemble it under fire — one of the most extraordinary engineering achievements in military history.

events.label: Column Clears Funchilin Pass
events.description: 14,000 troops, 1,000 vehicles, and all heavy equipment cross the repaired bridge and descend to the coastal plain. The PVA, exhausted and frostbitten, cannot prevent the crossing.

events.label: Hungnam Evacuation — Operation Christmas Cargo
events.description: 105,000 UN troops, 98,000 Korean civilian refugees, 17,500 vehicles, and 350,000 tons of supplies are evacuated by sea. The USS Meredith Victory alone carries 14,000 refugees in a single voyage.

events.label: Hungnam Port Demolished
events.description: After the last ship departs, engineers destroy port facilities, ammunition dumps, and infrastructure. Explosions are visible 50 miles away.

phases.annotation: The Hungnam evacuation is often called the 'Miracle of Christmas' — comparable to Dunkirk. The 1st Marine Division arrived at Hungnam as a cohesive, organized fighting force after 17 days of continuous combat at temperatures down to -40°C.

un-x-corps.note: Non-battle cold-weather casualties nearly equaled combat casualties

pva-9th-army.note: Three PVA divisions rendered completely combat-ineffective by frostbite alone; the 9th Army Group was withdrawn from combat for months

key_figures.name: Major General Oliver P. Smith
key_figures.significance: His deliberate advance pace and pre-positioning of supplies at Hagaru-ri — for which he was criticized — directly enabled the breakout.

key_figures.name: General Song Shilun
key_figures.significance: Achieved tactical surprise and encirclement but underestimated UN firepower and logistical resilience. His forces suffered more from cold than from combat.

key_figures.name: Lieutenant Colonel Don Faith
key_figures.significance: KIA while leading a desperate breakout on the east side. Awarded Medal of Honor posthumously.

sources.title: Breakout: The Chosin Reservoir Campaign — Martin Russ
USMC Historical Monograph: The Chosin Reservoir Campaign

wisdom.title: Logistics Wins Battles Before They Begin
wisdom.body: General Smith's unauthorized pre-positioning of supplies and building of the Hagaru-ri airstrip — against X Corps orders — is the single decision that saved the 1st Marine Division. The commander closest to reality must sometimes resist pressure from above.

wisdom.title: Never Discount Infiltration at Scale
wisdom.body: 120,000 PVA troops moved through mountains in sub-zero temperatures for two weeks, undetected by UN air reconnaissance. MacArthur's intelligence failure at Chosin is a defining case study in the danger of confirmation bias — seeing what you expect rather than what is there.

wisdom.title: Air Superiority as a Force Multiplier
wisdom.body: Marine Corsairs flying close air support were the decisive asymmetric advantage at Chosin. They negated the PVA's 4:1 numerical advantage. The difference in air power was not just tactical — it was the margin between survival and annihilation.

wisdom.title: Unit Cohesion Is the Ultimate Combat Multiplier
wisdom.body: Task Force Faith was destroyed; the Marine units survived. The structural difference was unit cohesion — the Marines had trained together, trusted their NCOs and commanders, and shared an ethos of never leaving men behind. RCT-31 was an ad-hoc assembly facing the same enemy in the same conditions.

wisdom.title: The Treadway Bridge: Improvise or Die
wisdom.body: The airdropped treadway bridge at Funchilin Pass has no precedent in military history. The willingness to attempt an untested solution under fire — and the engineering competence to execute it — is the difference between a fighting withdrawal and an annihilation.

wisdom.title: Tactical Defeat, Operational Victory
wisdom.body: The PVA achieved its tactical objective — encirclement. But the 1st Marine Division's organized withdrawal preserved a veteran fighting force that would continue the war. The measure of a military force is not whether it avoids encirclement, but whether it survives one.
